title: idleness is the pusher's clock
status: fixed after 0.4.1: a claim's last commit is dated by when GitHub received the push of its head, read once more where the first read may tell more, an entry after the run began dating it whatever heads it names, never earlier than the newest entry either read listed, and at the run's start in the run its own push started where no read dates it or a read dates it by an older push of the same head, and a claim on a head a release kept is released only where the board counts no release of it (github.head_since, coordinator.kept_released; DESIGN.md, 13)

steps.note: a's claim commit is dated 72 hours ahead
b pushes a commit dated 48 hours back

the activity, read for a's claim, lists a push after the run read the branch, from a's head to another, so a's branch had a commit now and its claim is held; b's last push came an hour ago, so it is held, though its head is dated 49 hours back; c's claim, idle 25 hours by either date, is released. Until the fix the committer dates decided, and b's claim was released here
read as the model holds it, a's claim reached GitHub 25 hours ago, so it is released, though its head says it is not made yet; until the fix it was held for 72 hours more

GitHub answers the first read of b's push with a 500, which it may answer later: the run reads once more, is answered, and dates b's claim by its push two hours ago, so it is held; read once, its committer date, 50 hours back, would have released it
the first read of b's push is answered before the activity lists it, the making newest: the run reads once more, which lists the push, and holds the claim

GitHub refuses every read of b's push for good, as for a token that may not read the activity: the run reads it once, dates it by its committer date, 50 hours back, and releases it, the spec's fallback, and its log says why
c pushes its released head again as claude/3, a push GitHub dates now
a pushes its released head again too and puts the label claimed back, which undoes the release for it
and so does b

released/3 keeps claude/3's head, so the release that kept it counts for the branch, though it came at 25 and the push at 26, and the board deletes it; dated by its push alone, or counted only from the push on, it would stand a day. claude/1 and claude/2, their releases undone, stand as claims
the owner takes the label claimed off b's issue again, so the release that kept its head counts again

a's branch has gone 25 hours without a push and the board counts no release of it, so the coordinator releases it again and the board deletes it, its head kept; with a release comment that counts holding a kept head, it would be held for good. b's the board counts released, so it is deleted with no second release, which a coordinator that read no kept head would make
a day after the board deleted claude/1 at its kept head, a pushes that head again as claude/1, a push that makes the branch again, which the activity lists after the board's delete

the first read of a's push is answered before the activity lists it, the board's delete at 51 newest, which moved the branch off that head before the run began: stale, so the run reads once more, which lists the push, and holds the claim; dated by the delete, a day back, the claim was released in the run its push started (F8's second review)

a's claim has gone 25 hours without a push and the board counts no release of it, so the coordinator releases it, and GitHub refuses the comment with a 422, having written none: the run puts the label claimed back, since the release comment of 51, which counts for a kept head whenever it came, is no comment this run wrote; taken for one, the labels stayed off with no word on the issue (F8's second review). A refusal, since F23's fix: after a 500 the run cannot tell whether GitHub wrote the comment and leaves the labels off, which on this kept head frees the claim by that earlier release
the next run releases it whole and the board deletes the branch, its head kept
c claims #3 anew, the board having deleted its kept head at 27
c's push moves claude/3 off its claim commit
a day later c drops that commit and pushes claude/3 back to its claim commit with a lease, a head the branch had before

the first read of c's push is answered before the activity lists it, c's push of 102 newest, which moved the branch off the head the run read a day before the run began: stale, so the run reads once more, which lists the forced push, and holds the claim; dated by the stale entry, it was released in the run its own push started (F8's second review)
c pushes a commit dated an hour back, at the minute of its forced push of 127

both reads of c's push are answered a push behind, the forced push of 127 newest, stale: the floor is that entry's time, the same minute as the commit's date, which is no later, so the committer date stands in, an hour back, the claim is held, and the log says the claim was read from its committer date; one that took such a floor for later says it was read from the floor (F8's fix check)
c pushes a commit dated 48 hours back

both reads of c's push are answered a push behind, c's push of 128 newest, stale: the floor, 128, later than the commit's date of 81, dates the claim, an hour idle, so it is held and the log says it was read from the floor; with the committer date standing in, two days back, the claim was released in the run its own push started, as before F8's fix check

the first read is answered a push behind, c's push of 128 newest, and GitHub refuses the one more with a 500: the floor is the newest entry either read listed, the first's, so the claim is held; taken from the last read alone, which listed none, the committer date stood in and released it

GitHub refuses the first read with a 500 and the one more lists a push after the run read the branch, from c's head to another: it came after the run began, so it dates the claim and the log says nothing of it; a second read judged with no moment of the run dates nothing by it, and its log says the claim was read from the floor at the same minute (F8's fix check)

the first read lists two pushes after the run read the branch, the newest naming c's head on neither side: it came after the run began, so it dates the claim and the run reads no more; one dating a fresh entry only where it moved the branch off the head reads again (F8's fix check)

the first read of c's push is two pushes behind, c's claim anew of 101 newest, and the one more one behind, c's push of 128 newest, as an activity catching up answers: the floor is the newest entry either read listed, 128, later than the commit's date of 81, so the claim is held; taken from the first read alone, or as the earlier of the two, 101, the claim was 28 hours idle and released while its holder was pushing (F8's third review)

GitHub refuses the first read of c's push with a 500 and the one more is a push behind, c's push of 128 newest: the floor is that read's, the one entry listed, later than the commit's date, so the claim is held, and the log says the activity lists no push of the head, the last read's word; taken from the first read alone, which listed nothing, the committer date stood in, two days back, and released the claim (F8's third review)

the first read of c's push lists the branch's delete after the run read it, at the run's minute, naming c's head as the head it took away: it came after the run began, so it dates the claim as a push after the read does, and the run reads no more; one that dates nothing by a fresh delete reads again and says in its log that the claim was read from the floor, at the same minute (F8's third review)
a claims #1 anew with a claim commit dated two days back; the push that makes the branch fires the board's create event

the run a's push started, the create event naming claude/1: both reads of a's push are answered before the activity lists the branch's making, so each lists the board's delete of 101 newest, a stale entry that dates nothing and is the floor, and the head is dated at the run's start and held, and the log says so; dated by that floor, 29 hours back, the claim was released in the run its own push started, as before F8's third review, as a fresh branch's would be by its committer date, its activity an empty list with no floor; c's claim, read after a's, is dated by its push of 129
c pushes on time

a day on, the activity lists a's push of 130, 25 hours back: the claim is released and its branch renamed, the run's start having held it one run alone; c's, pushed 24 hours back to the minute, is not yet idle
two days after its last push c drops its commits since its claim commit and pushes claude/3 back to it with a lease, the head the branch's making at 101 set

the run c's push started, the create event naming claude/3 standing in for the synchronize of c's pull request, which names the branch in the library and which the model does not play: the first read is two pushes behind and lists the branch's making of 101 newest, which set the head the run read, 80 hours back, an older push of that head, since the model's activity keeps a branch's making and its last two pushes; dated by it the claim was released in the run its own push started, as before F8's follow-up's second review, so the run dates it at its start and holds it, and its log says the newest push the activity lists of the head came before the run began
the next run, which no push of the branch started, reads the activity, which lists c's forced push of 181 newest, and holds the claim by it
